keywordRouting._note: Stream 2A 2026-09-09 (attack plan Phase 2A; essay docs/proposals/challenge-2026-09-08/C2-keyword-assignment.md). THE keyword router, as DATA. A control's DOM family says WHAT it is; fill vs verify vs actuate is the CALLER's INTENT, so it is three named slots here and two element fields (hint_fill / hint_verify) on the parsed element -- never a two-keyword string like 'TypeText / ClickText' baked into one `keyword`, which is what the parser emitted until this table landed. `metadataTypes` routes a DESCRIBE TYPE and WINS over the family when the org map has the field (CLAUDE.md: 'metadata routes the keyword, DOM is the backstop'); it is kept in step with tools/qforce-lite/predict.py:type_to_keyword by tools/recorder/tests/test_keyword_router_contract_2026_09_09.py, which also proves every keyword named here is a real rung in export._CRT_KW_MAP / writer._KW_MAP / library/index.json. A family with no keyword states a `reason` -- the tri-state rule, never silence. `_default` is the safety net: a family nobody has written a row for still yields a stated reason rather than an unexplained blank.

password.why: a masked text box; the read-back can only see the mask.

date.why: a bare date field is driveable through Set Datetime (date-only args); the describe type `date` routes to Type Text Clearing in metadataTypes.

datetime.why: one database value, a date input plus a 15-minute time combobox.

native-select.why: a real <select>. NOTE: v3 classifies these under family `select`, so this fieldFamilies entry currently matches nothing -- the row is kept so the name is routed the moment the family is renamed, and the mismatch is stated rather than hidden.

select.why: the family v3 actually assigns to a real <select> (see native-select).

checkbox.why: ClickCheckbox re-reads the input's `checked` property after clicking (confirm.py doctrine) -- that read-back is what makes it the right rung here and not a blind click.

radio.why: ClickCheckbox re-reads the input's `checked` property after clicking (confirm.py doctrine) -- that read-back is what makes it the right rung here and not a blind click.

switch.why: a role=switch is a checkbox with a switch skin; the checked property is still the state to read back.

slider.reason: no slider keyword has been proven live -- a drag gesture has no read-back rung yet.

file.reason: the upload lands as a ContentDocumentLink; asserting it is a records question, not a field read.

omni-output.reason: an OmniScript output field is a rendered value -- nothing to fill.

omni-edit-block.reason: an edit block is a repeating ROW container -- its rows are added with Omni Edit Block Add Row and the controls inside carry their own rungs.

omni-action.reason: an OmniScript action is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

omni-step-nav.reason: step navigation is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

aura-picklist.why: real QWeb has no Aura branch -- the plain PickList rung does not drive Aura's open gesture.

aura-date.why: Aura's date input is a native text input with a JS mask.

row.why: a row is addressed by its key column's value; Select Table Row and Click Table Row Action Where take that key.

rowgroup.reason: a rowgroup is table structure, not a control -- its rows carry the rungs.

columnheader.reason: a column header is an ARGUMENT to the table rungs (the `col` of Get Table Cell Where / Set Table Cell), not a control driven on its own.

rowheader.why: a row header is the row's key cell -- the value the table rungs take as the row key.

button.reason: a button is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

link.reason: a link is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

tab.reason: a tab is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

tabpanel.reason: a tab PANEL is the content its tab reveals, not a control.

tree.reason: a tree item is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

path.reason: a path stage is actuated, then asserted with Verify Path Stage.

progress.reason: a progress marker is rendered status -- assert it as text, never as a field value.

console-subtab.reason: a console workspace tab is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

console-tertiary-tab.reason: a tertiary tab is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

utility-bar-item.reason: a utility-bar item is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

split-view-row.reason: a split-view row is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

carousel-slide.reason: a carousel slide is actuated by a click rung (ClickText / ClickItem, both already offered as locator options); it holds no value to fill or assert.

menu.reason: a menu is a container; its items are the controls.

listbox.reason: a listbox is the dropdown a combobox/picklist opens -- drive the control, not its popup.

option.reason: an option is a VALUE inside a picklist/combobox listbox -- it is the argument to PickList / ComboBox, never a control of its own.

radiogroup.why: the group is driven by clicking the member option.

pill.reason: a pill displays a chosen value; set it through the control that produced it.

iframe.reason: an iframe is a FRAME, not a control -- QWeb auto-penetrates frames.

custom.reason: an unrecognised custom element has no proven keyword -- check SHAPES-GUIDE.md before assuming a click drives it.

label.reason: a label NAMES a control -- it is the locator argument, not a target.

presentation.reason: role=presentation is explicitly not a control.

tablist.reason: a tablist is a container; its tabs are the controls.

_default.reason: no keywordRouting row is declared for this family -- add one once a keyword is proven for the shape. Stated absence, never silence.

date.why: predict.type_to_keyword('date') is 'certain' on type_text_clearing -- a date field is typed as MM/DD/YYYY. Set Datetime is the DOM-family answer for a datepicker that also renders a time sibling, which is a different question from the describe type.

datetime.why: a datetime is a COMPOUND control -- one database value, a date input plus a 15-minute time combobox under one legend.

combobox.why: describe type `combobox` is a picklist that also accepts free text; pick_list drives the listbox half. The free-text half has no keyword on any org we own.

encryptedstring.reason: the platform returns the MASKED value to describe, SOQL and the rendered form for anyone without View Encrypted Data, so no read-back can prove what landed -- the fill is routed, the assert is COULD-NOT-CHECK.

address.reason: a compound address is several sub-fields under one legend; there is no single-value assert rung for it.

location.reason: geolocation persistence after Save is could-not-check (BACKLOG-61-EVIDENCE.md SS3); the fill mechanism is live-measured.

time.reason: no time-only keyword exists. Set Datetime drives a DATE input plus a time combobox, and routing a time field to it would type into a date box that is not there -- predict.type_to_keyword('time') states the same gap.

base64.reason: a Blob body is never an editable control on a create/edit form -- the platform renders no input for it. A gap by design, not a missing rung.

id.reason: an Id is never an editable control on a create/edit form.

reference.why: the PLAIN-lookup case only. predict.type_to_keyword splits `reference` by API NAME through chains.REFERENCE_SUBKINDS (OwnerId / CreatedById / LastModifiedById / RecordTypeId are not plain lookups and route nowhere); a DOM template has no API name, so this row is allowlisted in the router contract test rather than pretending to make that split.

hostInnerCollapse._why: interop T16 2026-09-07, read by v3._collapse_host_inner. T14 priced v3's missing dedup pass at 27.1 points of precision: 87 of its 91 false positives were the SAME control emitted twice -- li[role=treeitem] plus the <a> inside it (57 in one Setup nav tree), and a <label> beside the control it captions under a lightning-input-field host (11 in Zoo_Aura_v3). A drop happens ONLY when a second element is provably the same control (nested within maxDepth AND same label, or a caption-family element duplicating a real control under a shared ancestor). Different labels mean different controls -- the tree grid's columnheader contains its column-action button and both survive. Set enabled:false to restore the pre-T16 output byte for byte. | stream V1 2026-09-08 added captionTags: a <label> is a caption because of its TAG. An OmniStudio radio/checkbox option is a <label>+<input> pair under one *-group host, so both halves classify as omni-radio/omni-checkbox and captionFamilies (which keys on FAMILY) never fired -- 5 duplicate false positives appeared the moment collapseToHost was turned off for those groups.

note_labelPolicy: interop T10 2026-09-07: the label POLICY layer, read by tools/interop/resources/pythonDom/element_compiler.py through DomConfiguration. labelPrecedence names are the label_source values the compiler emits; the first rung that resolves wins. Omit a key here and the compiler falls back to its own class attribute.
note_hintOrderByLabelSource: interop T17 2026-09-07: mirrors salesforce-lightning.json (see there for full rationale) -- ClickItem before ClickText for title_attr/aria_label labels unless the label is also the element's rendered text.
note_labelPrecedence: labelPrecedence: `inner_text` is FIRST as of the wave-2 review close (stream P1, 2026-09-07, findings F6/R12). THE LABEL IS WHAT A PERSON SEES -- a title tooltip or an ARIA accessible name labels a control only when nothing visible does. Measured before the move: 110 elements across the 144-capture corpus carried a title_attr label while their own rendered_text said something else. `inner_text` only produces a value for button/a/role=button, so form controls are unaffected and an icon-only control still falls through to title_attr. `assistive_text` is last: never visible, but on a chevron-only button it is the only handle there is.
note_assistiveTextClassFragments: assistiveTextClassFragments: class fragments marking SCREEN-READER-ONLY text. Text inside one of these is stripped from every visible-label candidate and is only offered by the last `assistive_text` rung of labelPrecedence, with its own label_source. Added by the wave-2 review close (stream P1, 2026-09-07, finding F11) -- was a literal tuple in element_compiler.py, which is why 'inner_text' concatenated 'Show more navigation items' onto the visible '* More'.

labelSourceCaveats.assistive_text: This label came from SCREEN-READER-ONLY markup (an slds-assistive-text / sr-only span) -- nothing on this control is visible to a sighted person, so a rendered-text search may not find it. Confirm the click landed (read-back or the optical witness) before trusting this step.

note_labelSourceCaveats: labelSourceCaveats: a caveat appended to every hint whose locator IS the label, keyed by the labelPrecedence rung that produced that label. Added by the wave-2 review close (stream P1, 2026-09-07, finding F11 / L2-R08): a hint built on assistive text must say so rather than read as if the string were visible on the page.
note_innerTextExcludedRoles: innerTextExcludedRoles: roles whose own rendered text is the control's VALUE, not its NAME, so the `inner_text` rung (first, since the wave-2 review close) must never claim them. A Lightning picklist is <button role="combobox" aria-label="Industry">--None--</button>; without this key the field's label became '--None--'. Added by stream P1, 2026-09-07, after its own test caught the regression in the org map's metadata->control routing.

groupCaptions._why: stream V1 2026-09-08, read by v3._group_captions. A radio group, a checkbox group and a dual listbox are ONE field in the layout and one control in a test step, but the group's name lives only in its <legend>/slds-form-element__legend node -- every member input carries the OPTION's name instead, so v3 emitted no element at all for 'Zoo Radio', 'Zoo Multi Select' or 'Zoo Tags' (3 of the 13 recall misses named in docs/recorder/evidence/v3-decision-2026-09-07.md). v1 and T14's hand-labelled ground truth both list the group. The caption inherits the family of the members it captions, so no new family name enters family-map.json, and it is skipped when an element already carries that label. Set enabled:false to restore the pre-V1 output.

ownTextOutranksNearestLabel._why: stream V1 2026-09-08, read by v3._label. The 'nearest' ancestor scan renamed elements that already say their own name: the dual listbox's chosen options both came back as 'Chosen' (the listbox's legend) instead of 'Billing'/'Onboarding', and the rich-text colour picker came back as 'Zoo Rich Text' (the FIELD's label) instead of 'Choose a color. Current color:'. That is CLAUDE.md's label-vs-value failure in its container form -- 3 of the 13 recall misses in docs/recorder/evidence/v3-decision-2026-09-07.md plus one duplicate false positive. v3's fallback ladder already carried this guard ('a button/link's own text is always the correct signal'); this extends it to the ancestor scan. aria-label, title and label[for] still outrank own text -- only the nearby-form-element-label guess is dropped. | excludeFamilies: a CONTAINER is named by its legend, never by the text of the things inside it -- without this the dual listbox's 'Chosen' side renamed itself 'Billing Onboarding' (seen firing, one control lost). useAssistiveText: the rich-text colour picker has NO visible text at all; its own name is a screen-reader span, which is still ITS name and still outranks the field label six hops up.

hostInnerKeepsOwnName._why: stream V1 2026-09-08, read by v3's host-collapse branch. collapseToHost keeps ONE element per component host, which is right for an input and its clear/toggle button -- but wrong when the inner node carries its OWN distinct name. The OmniStudio date picker's icon button is title='Select Date' with aria-label='Zoo Date' (the field's name, inherited), and the typeahead's Edit button is named only by an assistive-text span; both were dropped as dup_inputs and both are separate controls in T14's ground truth AND in v1 (2 of the 13 recall misses in docs/recorder/evidence/v3-decision-2026-09-07.md). A name equal to the host control's own label is NOT a distinct name and is still collapsed, so the input+clear-button case is unchanged. Set enabled:false to restore the pre-V1 output.
